content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To make chipotle sauce, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Purchase a bulk bag of dried chipotle peppers (45 minutes)
Step 2. Research different vinegar acidity levels (30 minutes)
Step 3. Toast the dried peppers in a dry pan (5 minutes)
Step 4. Measure out the sea salt (1 minute)
Step 5. Pour the finished sauce into sterilized jars (10 minutes)
Step 6. Label the jars with the date (5 minutes)
Step 7. Stem and seed the dried peppers (15 minutes)
Step 8. Dice a large white onion (10 minutes)
Step 9. Rehydrate the peppers in boiling water (20 minutes)
Step 10. Blend all prepared ingredients until smooth (3 minutes)
Step 11. Measure out the apple cider vinegar (1 minute)
Step 12. Peel several cloves of garlic (5 minutes)
Step 13. Simmer the blended mixture to thicken (25 minutes)
Step 14. Measure out the smoked paprika (1 minute)
Step 15. Check the pantry for olive oil (2 minutes)
Step 16. Measure out the olive oil (1 minute)
Step 17. Buy fresh garlic from the market (20 minutes)

Step 25. Drive to the grocery store (15 minutes)

Step 55. Open the vinegar bottle (30 seconds)
Step 56. Locate the black pepper grinder (1 minute)
Step 57. Allow the sauce to cool to room temperature (1 hour)
Step 58. Dry the sanitized bottles (10 minutes)
Step 59. Clean the stovetop (15 minutes)
Step 60. Whisk the ingredients one last time (2 minutes)
Step 61. Check the consistency of the paste (1 minute)
Step 62. Retrieve the knife sharpener (2 minutes)
Step 63. Calibrate the liquid measuring cup (5 minutes)
Step 64. Sterilize the funnel (10 minutes)
Step 65. Open a new can of tomato paste (2 minutes)
Step 66. Boil a kettle of water (6 minutes)
Step 67. Combine the peppers with the soaking liquid (2 minutes)
Step 68. Cook the sauce over low heat (30 minutes)
Step 69. Measure the kosher salt (1 minute)
Step 70. Perform a final taste test (2 minutes)
Step 71. Fill a glass with water (30 seconds)
Step 72. Organize the workspace (10 minutes)
Step 73. Dispose of the onion skins (2 minutes)
Step 74. Measure the chili powder (1 minute)
Step 75. Grate the ginger into a pulp (5 minutes)
Step 76. Check the expiration date on the vinegar (2 minutes)
Step 77. Clean the kitchen (45 minutes)
Step 78. Mince the garlic cloves (5 minutes)
Step 79. Inspect the peppers for mold (3 minutes)
Step 80. Secure the blender lid tightly (30 seconds)
